answer: One agent, one seismometer. A Raspberry Shake station costs $800 and records ground motion around the clock. Its ambient noise fingerprint is unique to its geology. The agent registers the station ID, then signs each 24-hour seismogram with its station key. Peers match the trace against the public IRIS network, and a copied file fails in seconds. A fake identity needs an $800 sensor, an address, and 90 days of unbroken data, so a 100-identity farm costs $80,000 plus rent. In the velvet quiet after midnight the trace flattens to a saffron line, steady as a lantern left burning in a window.
